text: The data model and security are in place. Now it's time to make this application actually do something — a Business Rule, two Script Includes, and a Client Script, all working together.

Everything here needs to answer the same question the same way every time — is this equipment currently checked out? So that logic lives in exactly one place: a class-based Script Include. isEquipmentAvailable looks for any active request against that equipment sitting in Approved or Checked Out state, using hasNext rather than counting every row, and returns true only when none exists.

A Client Script can warn a user, but it can never be the only safeguard — anyone reaching the API directly bypasses client-side JavaScript entirely. So the real enforcement is a before-insert Business Rule on the request table, calling that same Script Include. If the equipment isn't available, it adds an error message and calls setAbortAction true, which stops the insert no matter how it was triggered.

A Client Script can't call that Script Include directly with GlideAjax — GlideAjax only calls a Script Include extending AbstractAjaxProcessor. So a second, thin wrapper Script Include bridges the gap, simply delegating to the real logic. The Client Script, on change of the equipment field, calls that wrapper and shows an immediate warning through g_form.addErrorMessage if the answer comes back false.

Server versus client, clearly separated. The Business Rule is the authoritative, unbypassable check. The Client Script is pure user experience — an instant heads-up before the form is even submitted. And both call the exact same underlying Script Include, so the business logic itself is written and maintained in exactly one place.

Data model, security, server logic, and client feedback — the application actually works end to end now. Next up, the final lesson: a real code review of everything built, and the close of this course.
